prompt: Research one critical-minerals copper-scarcity investment idea.

inputs.seed_claim: Structural copper scarcity is a concentrate, cathode-availability, and capital-discipline thesis rather than a perpetual spot-price thesis; low-cost miners and electrical OEMs with pricing power are the cleanest beneficiaries.
inputs.drivers: Grid and data-centre investment; EVs and electrification; declining grades; long mine lead times; project capex and permitting; concentrate availability and treatment charges; China demand; recycling and aluminium substitution.
inputs.value_chain: Copper miners and concentrate producers; smelters and refiners; grid and electrical OEMs; EPC builders; copper-intensive industrial customers; substitutes and hedges.
inputs.supporting_evidence: The seed cites an IEA potential supply shortfall near 25% by 2035 and benchmark treatment charges near zero, with SCCO, FCX, ETN, GEV, and VRT as hypotheses.
inputs.invalidation: Recycling, aluminium substitution, faster permitting, project restarts, weak China demand, or demand destruction from high prices could compress scarcity and downstream margins.
